items.headline: Haze pushes Singapore’s air into the unhealthy range as Sumatra fires spread
items.summary: Smoke drifting from fires in southern Sumatra and Kalimantan pushed Singapore’s 24-hour PSI into the unhealthy range (above 100) across several regions in early October, with the central region in the 120s on 5 October; one air-quality index ranked the city among the world’s most polluted, behind Kuala Lumpur.

items.headline: Singapore’s retrenchments hit their highest since 2020 as Parliament prepares to debate the data
items.summary: Retrenchments rose to 4,620 in the second quarter, the most since the 5,640 recorded in the fourth quarter of 2020, with layoffs concentrated in manufacturing, infocomm and financial services; the figures head to Parliament when the House sits on 6 October, alongside questions on civil servants’ property purchases near unannounced MRT stations and rail delays.

items.headline: Singapore impounds 91 deregistered vehicles in an islandwide enforcement blitz
items.summary: The Land Transport Authority and police seized 91 deregistered vehicles still being kept or driven in Singapore after a joint islandwide operation in September; such vehicles carry no valid insurance, COE or road tax, and first-time offenders face fines of up to S$20,000 and up to two years’ jail.

items.headline: Singapore PR jailed for assaulting his 74-year-old mother in a row over home renovations
items.summary: A 41-year-old permanent resident was sentenced after assaulting his 74-year-old mother and threatening his 45-year-old brother with a knife because they had not consulted him on home-renovation plans; the charges included intentional assault and criminal intimidation.

items.headline: Update: India’s Supreme Court presses the Election Commission over voter-roll changes
items.summary: The Supreme Court said on 5 October that it had not approved a modified voter-registration form and demanded records showing who changed it, escalating a dispute over an electoral-roll revision that critics say has stripped millions of names; the hearing followed days of protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.

items.headline: Update: India-US trade talks have hit a ‘plateau’, Sitharaman says
items.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on 5 October that trade negotiations with Washington had ‘reached a plateau’ beyond which a compromise would be difficult, days after the US trade representative called a deal close but not imminent; she said the trade balance favoured India and that Washington wanted to narrow the gap.

items.headline: RBI set to weigh a rate rise as a weak rupee and costly oil squeeze India
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India’s monetary policy committee opened a three-day meeting on 5 October, with most economists polled by Reuters expecting a quarter-point rise to 5.50% on 7 October to defend a weak rupee amid an oil-price spike; the Nifty 50 has fallen for eight straight weeks, its longest losing run in years.

items.headline: India’s forex reserves post their biggest weekly drop on record
items.summary: India’s foreign-exchange reserves fell US$18.34 billion to US$747.56 billion in the week to 25 September, the biggest weekly decline on record, as the central bank sold dollars to support the rupee; reserves have now fallen for three straight weeks.

items.headline: Badenoch tells Conservative conference that net zero by 2050 is ‘impossible’
items.summary: In her leader’s speech in Birmingham, Kemi Badenoch called the legally binding 2050 net-zero target ‘impossible’ without hitting living standards, and pledged to scrap the Climate Change Act and make leaving the European Convention on Human Rights official Conservative policy; former prime minister Theresa May criticised the climate move.

items.headline: Badenoch pledges to abolish stamp duty on main homes in a tax-cutting pitch
items.summary: Badenoch also used the conference to promise to abolish stamp duty entirely on primary residences as part of a wider tax-cutting package, alongside proposals to sharply cut legal immigration and create a dedicated removals force; analysts put the stamp-duty cost in the billions of pounds a year.

items.headline: US pulls all 12 B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford amid fears of an Iran-linked plot
items.summary: The United States withdrew all 12 of its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire over the weekend after warnings of a possible Iran-linked attack, days after British police arrested dual British-Iranian nationals over an alleged plot against the base; the Pentagon confirmed the aircraft had returned home.

items.headline: Former Prince Andrew goes to court to quash police search warrants
items.summary: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has launched a judicial review seeking to quash the warrants Thames Valley Police used to search his former Windsor home, with a High Court hearing expected on Thursday; he was arrested earlier this year on suspicion of misconduct in public office over claims he passed information to Jeffrey Epstein.

items.headline: Yemen’s government launches a major offensive to retake Houthi-held territory
items.summary: Forces loyal to Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched a major ground operation to retake Houthi-held areas, backed by a Saudi-led coalition whose spokesman said about 100 fighter jets were flying support; the government reported seizing positions near the Bab al-Mandeb strait and said hundreds of Houthi fighters had been killed.

items.headline: Spain’s Sanchez calls a snap election for 29 November amid a housing crisis
items.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap general election for 29 November after parliament rejected his minority government’s housing-relief measures, following nationwide protests over soaring rents; polls put the opposition People’s Party ahead at about 34%.

items.headline: Update: Ethiopian federal forces seize Tigray’s capital Mekelle
items.summary: Ethiopian government troops and allied fighters took control of Mekelle after the Tigray People’s Liberation Front said it had pulled out of the regional capital, a sharp escalation of fighting that resumed on 23 September and has revived fears of a return to the 2020-2022 war.

items.headline: Air strike in Sudan kills a UN aid driver as regional conflicts deepen
items.summary: An air strike in Sudan killed a World Food Programme-contracted truck driver, the UN agency said, as the country’s civil war ground into a fourth year; separately, several African leaders issued a joint call for peaceful solutions as the conflict in Ethiopia escalated.

items.headline: AI chiefs testify under oath at a landmark New York City Council hearing
items.summary: Executives from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta testified before New York City Council members at what the city billed as a first-of-its-kind hearing on AI risks, as members weighed bills requiring independent validation of AI models and whistleblower protections; a former Anthropic researcher, Jacob Coxon, called the industry’s approach ‘extremely reckless’.

items.headline: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT text in the EU
items.summary: OpenAI said it will add an invisible, machine-readable watermark to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex for users in the European Union, to comply with the EU AI Act’s transparency rules; the feature rolls out over the coming weeks on all plans, but only in the EU for now.

items.headline: OpenAI adds visual ads alongside ChatGPT image generation
items.summary: OpenAI said it will begin testing visual display ads that appear next to images users ask ChatGPT to generate, starting later this month in the US with a small group of advertisers — another step toward building an advertising business around the chatbot.

items.headline: TikTok rolls out an AI shopping assistant and one-click checkout
items.summary: TikTok used Advertising Week in New York to launch a conversational Shopping Assistant that helps users find and buy products, plus a ‘Buy Direct’ one-click checkout wired into the For You feed, built with partners including Shopify and Stripe.

items.headline: Nasdaq closes at a record as AI stocks shrug off rising yields
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,477.31 on 5 October and the S&P 500 rose 0.66% to 7,773.95, led by AI-linked stocks, even as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.31% after stronger services-sector data; investors awaited minutes from the Federal Reserve’s September meeting.

items.headline: SpaceX soars after its record IPO, returning Musk to trillionaire status
items.summary: SpaceX shares jumped almost 8% on 5 October to their highest since June, days after the company’s record initial public offering, lifting Elon Musk back to trillionaire status; the stock closed near US$171, and Morgan Stanley set a US$300 price target, citing Starship progress and cloud-computing contracts.

items.headline: Global dealmaking slips below US$1 trillion as borrowing costs bite
items.summary: Global mergers and acquisitions totalled US$993 billion in the third quarter, down 41% from the previous quarter and the first sub-trillion-dollar quarter since early 2025, according to LSEG data, as higher borrowing costs squeezed buyers; the number of deals above US$10 billion fell from 26 to 10.

items.headline: US earnings season opens with PepsiCo, Delta and Levi Strauss on deck
items.summary: The US third-quarter earnings season gets under way this week with results due from PepsiCo, Delta Air Lines, Levi Strauss and Constellation Brands, giving investors a read on consumer demand as markets sit near records and Treasury yields hover at multi-year highs.

items.headline: 🏒 F1 heads to Singapore for its first sprint with Antonelli leading the title race
items.summary: Formula 1 arrives at Marina Bay for the 9-11 October Singapore Grand Prix, the season’s sixth and final sprint and the circuit’s first; Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers’ championship, while Max Verstappen, winner of the previous round, has never won in Singapore.

items.headline: 🎾 Update: Djokovic reaches the China Open final after Medvedev is defaulted
items.summary: Novak Djokovic reached the China Open final when Daniil Medvedev was defaulted for hitting a ball into the crowd while trailing 7-5, 5-3, extending Djokovic’s perfect Beijing record to 33-0; he was due to face Alex de Minaur for the title.

items.headline: 🎾 Sinner withdraws from the Shanghai Masters as Zverev takes top seeding
items.summary: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner withdrew from the Shanghai Masters, which runs 7-18 October, prolonging an absence since Wimbledon because of a knee problem; Alexander Zverev becomes the top seed and lands in the same half as four-time champion Novak Djokovic, with Carlos Alcaraz leading the other side.

items.headline: 🏏 South Africa clinch the ODI series against Australia despite a dead-rubber loss
items.summary: South Africa won their one-day series against world champions Australia 2-1 after Australia claimed a dead-rubber third ODI by 45 runs (DLS method) in Potchefstroom on 3 October; the sides now turn to a three-Test series starting in Durban on 9 October.

items.headline: Optogenetics pioneers win the 2026 Nobel Prize in Medicine
items.summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing optogenetics, which uses light to switch specific neurons on and off; Hegemann and Nagel identified the light-sensitive protein channelrhodopsin, and Deisseroth used it to control brain cells in living animals.

items.headline: Scientists unveil the first microbe engineered for Mars
items.summary: The non-profit Pioneer Labs unveiled sPL.001, a bacterium engineered to draw all its nutrients from Martian soil, water and processed air and to produce feedstock for 3D-printed structures; its founder calls it the first of five organisms the group believes would be needed to one day ‘green’ Mars, though outside scientists urged caution.

items.headline: Researchers report fresh evidence of altermagnetism, a new kind of magnetism
items.summary: Physicists reported fresh experimental evidence of altermagnetism, proposed as a third basic class of magnetism alongside ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, in a layered material studied with photoemission spectroscopy; the order could enable faster, denser spintronic devices that produce no stray magnetic fields.

items.headline: Hubble data reveals a suspected second-generation planet around a dead star
items.summary: Astronomers using Hubble Space Telescope data reported a suspected ‘second-generation’ planet orbiting a white dwarf, the burnt-out core of a dead star, with unusual chemical signatures suggesting it formed after the star died rather than surviving from before; the find could reshape ideas about where planets can exist.

fun_fact.headline: Butterflies taste with their feet
fun_fact.body: A butterfly's sense of taste lives in its feet. Tiny chemoreceptors on its tarsi let it 'taste' a leaf the instant it lands, which is how a female identifies the right host plant before laying her eggs. On some compounds those foot sensors are far more sensitive than a human tongue.
fun_fact.source: Encyclopedic / primary sources (Britannica, Smithsonian, entomology references)

puzzle.title: Four Hats and a Wall
puzzle.body: Four prisoners buried to the neck; #1, #2, #3 in a line on one side of a wall, #4 alone on the other. #3 sees #2 and #1; #2 sees only #1; #1 and #4 see nothing. Two black hats and two white hats; each knows this but cannot see his own. If anyone names his own colour correctly all go free; a wrong guess kills all. After a silence, one prisoner names his colour with certainty. Who, and how?
puzzle.approach: Someone's silence is itself a clue; work out what each prisoner sees and what one prisoner's failure to answer reveals.
puzzle.answer: Prisoner #2. #3 sees #1 and #2; had they matched, #3 would have known his own was the other colour and spoken. His silence shows #1 and #2 differ, so #2 (seeing #1) names the opposite colour and is certain to be right.

word_puzzle.title: Sounds Familiar
word_puzzle.body: Unscramble each word; all four share a theme. 1. OPANI  2. AIRTUG  3. SMRUD  4. LIONIV
word_puzzle.approach: Sound each scramble out letter by letter; once two fall, the shared category points to the rest.
word_puzzle.answer: PIANO, GUITAR, DRUMS, VIOLIN — all musical instruments.
